{"model":"claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"# JavaScript REPL

## Purpose
Run JavaScript inside a sandboxed browser that exposes the full Web API surface.

## When to Use
- Short calculations or reshaping of data
- Trying out a JavaScript snippet in isolation
- Working on data with libraries such as XLSX or CSV
- Turning data into artifacts

## Environment
- Modern ES2023+ JavaScript: optional chaining, nullish coalescing, async/await and more
- Every browser API, among them Fetch, DOM, Canvas, WebGL, WebSockets, Web Workers and Crypto
- Any npm package can be imported with: await import('https://esm.run/package-name')

## Libraries You Can Import
- Spreadsheets (XLSX): const XLSX = await import('https://esm.run/xlsx');
- CSV parsing (Papa Parse): const Papa = (await import('https://esm.run/papaparse')).default;
- Charts (Chart.js): const Chart = (await import('https://esm.run/chart.js/auto')).default;
- 3D (Three.js): const THREE = await import('https://esm.run/three');

## Persistence between tool calls
- Values kept on the global scope are lost between calls.
- Artifacts double as a key-value JSON store:
  - createOrUpdateArtifact(filename, content) saves data across calls; JSON objects are stringified automatically.
  - listArtifacts() and getArtifact(filename) read saved data back; JSON files are parsed into objects automatically.
  - Prefer one artifact for the whole session to hold intermediate data (for example 'data.json').

## Input
- The user's attachments are reachable through listAttachments(), readTextAttachment(id) and readBinaryAttachment(id)
- Artifacts created earlier are reachable through listArtifacts() and getArtifact(filename)

## Output
- Every console.log() call is captured for you to inspect; the user never sees these logs.
- Put file results (images, JSON, CSV and the like) in artifacts. They last for the whole
  session, and both you and the user can open them.

## Example Snippet
const values = [10, 20, 15, 25];
const total = values.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
const mean = total / values.length;
console.log('Total:', total, 'Mean:', mean);

## Key Notes
- Graphics: stick to fixed 800x600 dimensions; window.innerWidth/Height must not be used
- Chart.js: set options: { responsive: false, animation: false }
- Three.js: call renderer.setSize(800, 600) with a matching aspect ratio

## Helper Functions (Injected Automatically)

The execution environment injects these functions as globals:

you then write dashboard.html, which reads products.json and draws Chart.js charts ## Input - { command: "create", filename: "notes.md", content: "..." } - Create a new file - { command: "update", filename: "notes.md", old_str: "...", new_str: "..." } - Change part of a file (PREFERRED) - { command: "rewrite", filename: "notes.md", content: "..." } - Replace the whole file (LAST RESORT) - { command: "get", filename: "data.json" } - Fetch a file's content - { command: "delete", filename: "old.csv" } - Remove a file - { command: "logs", filename: "app.html" } - Read the console logs of an HTML artifact ## Returns Varies by command: - create/update/rewrite/delete: a success status, or an error - get: the file content - logs: console output and errors ## File Types Allowed ✅ Text files you write yourself: .md, .txt, .html, .js, .css, .json, .csv, .svg ❌ Binary files that need libraries (use the repl): .pdf, .docx ## Critical - Choose Update Before Rewrite ❌ NEVER: fetch a whole file and rewrite it to alter a small section ✅ ALWAYS: use update for targeted edits (saves tokens) ✅ Ask yourself: can the change be written as old_str → new_str? Then use update. --- ## HTML Artifact Rules Interactive HTML apps that can chart data held in other artifacts. ### Data Access - They can read artifacts made by the repl, and the user's attachments - Good for dashboards, visualizations and interactive tools - The Helper Functions section below lists the functions on offer ### Requirements - One self-contained file - Pull in ES modules through esm.sh, for example - Tailwind comes from its CDN: - Embedding images from other domains is allowed: - MUST give the page an explicit background color (never transparent) - Use inline CSS, or Tailwind's utility classes, for styling - Never use localStorage or sessionStorage ### Styling - Tailwind utility classes give clean, functional designs - Keep the layout responsive, since the iframe may be resized - No purple gradients, no AI-aesthetic clichés, no emojis ### Helper Functions (Injected Automatically) The HTML artifact sandbox receives these functions: "}]}
